summary: Small set of services: React (Vite SPA) (web) + Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform (Android + iOS) on Java 21/25 LTS + Spring Boot with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 — ap-south-1 (Mumbai) (multi-AZ / zone-redundant HA), hosted on AWS ECS on Fargate (+ Application Load Balancer) — ap-south-1 (Mumbai). Estimated $1130-6219/month.

frontend.choice: React (Vite SPA) (web) + Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform (Android + iOS)
frontend.justification: Web: React (Vite SPA) — Rich interactive app screens; team already writes typescript for the UI; same React component model as a React Native mobile app; good security (priority 5/5); good low running cost (priority 2/5). Mobile: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform — Team already writes java, kotlin for the mobile app; one codebase for Android and iOS; good security (priority 5/5); good maintainability (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: Learning curve 4/5 for a senior team (team.experience). React (Vite SPA) is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 3/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 2.4 points behind. Known limit of Angular: steeper learning curve; 24-month support per major.

Learning curve 3/5 for a senior team (team.experience). React (Vite SPA) is stronger on: good low running cost (priority 2/5) (priorities.cost). Overall 2.4 points behind. Known limit of Next.js: server runtime needed for SSR; more moving parts than a static site.

Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform is stronger on: good performance (priority 3/5) (priorities.performance); good security (priority 5/5) (priorities.security). Overall 0.3 points behind. Known limit of React Native: jS runtime overhead on very low-end phones.

Weaker performance (priority 3/5) (priorities.performance). Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform is stronger on: good security (priority 5/5) (priorities.security). Overall 8.3 points behind. Known limit of Ionic Capacitor: webView performance on low-end devices.

tradeoffs: Client-rendered pages are weak for SEO
iOS tooling less mature than native Swift

React (Vite SPA) is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 3/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Trade-off accepted: Client-rendered pages are weak for SEO.

database.choice: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 — ap-south-1 (Mumbai) (multi-AZ / zone-redundant HA)
database.justification: Strict ACID transactions for money movement and ledger postings; good security (priority 5/5); good maintainability (priority 4/5). The 99.95% target uses a standby in a second zone with automatic failover and point-in-time recovery. Automated backups and snapshots stay in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) (no cross-region copies), as RBI localisation requires.

alternatives.why_not: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 is stronger on: good low running cost (priority 2/5) (priorities.cost). Overall 3.2 points behind. Known limit of Amazon RDS for SQL Server: licence cost outside Azure SQL; Windows-centric tooling.

Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 is stronger on: good security (priority 5/5) (priorities.security); good maintainability (priority 4/5) (priorities.maintainability). Overall 9.7 points behind. Known limit of Amazon RDS for MySQL 8.4: 8.0 moved to Sustaining Support (Apr 2026); no row-level security.
Excluded: a separate vendor outside the explicit cloud_preference aws (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Vertical write scaling; sharding needs extensions

hosting.choice: AWS ECS on Fargate (+ Application Load Balancer) — ap-south-1 (Mumbai)
hosting.justification: Satisfies the hard constraints (cloud_preference aws, managed_cloud (no servers to patch), data_residency india -> ap-south-1 (Mumbai)). Runs across availability zones for the 99.95% target; good security (priority 5/5); good scalability (priority 4/5).

alternatives.choice: AWS Elastic Beanstalk (managed platform on EC2)
alternatives.why_not: The EC2/VM operating system stays in your patching and hardening scope for rbi_localisation, pci_dss, iso27001 (compliance). AWS ECS on Fargate (+ Application Load Balancer) is stronger on: good security (priority 5/5) (priorities.security). Overall 2.1 points behind. Known limit of AWS Elastic Beanstalk: you still pay for and size the EC2 instances underneath.

Spring Boot is a long-running JVM/.NET server: slow cold starts and per-invocation connection pools on functions (team.languages); ~10,000 concurrent users would open relational connections per function instance; needs a connection proxy (scale.peak_concurrent_users). Overall 7.8 points behind. Known limit of AWS Lambda + API Gateway: cold starts hurt tight p95 targets.
Excluded: runs on gcp, but cloud_preference is aws (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Load balancer and NAT add fixed monthly cost
More AWS concepts (VPC, IAM, task definitions) than a PaaS

supporting.choice: Razorpay (UPI, cards, netbanking) — RazorpayX Payouts for UPI loan disbursals to borrowers; Subscriptions with UPI AutoPay / e-mandate for recurring collections
supporting.justification: The description requires UPI. Hosted checkout keeps card data off your servers (PCI DSS SAQ A scope when fully outsourced). Payment confirmation is trusted only from signed server-side webhooks. For lending, disburse straight to the borrower's bank account and collect repayments directly into the lender's (regulated entity's) account — no pooled pass-through accounts (RBI Digital Lending Directions 2025). pci_dss: the gateway is PCI DSS Level 1; your scope still covers the pages that embed checkout.

alternatives.why_not: comparable Indian gateway; Razorpay chosen for combined UPI + payouts + subscriptions documentation
India accounts are invite-based and UPI coverage is narrower

tradeoffs: Per-transaction fees (~2% domestic cards) are charged on revenue, not in the infrastructure band

assumptions: Hosting AWS ECS on Fargate (+ Application Load Balancer): $200-900/month at the 'medium' tier.
Database Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17: $270-1400/month (HA doubles instances).
Availability ≥99.95%: at least two app instances across zones.
auth: Amazon Cognito user pool + Amazon SNS SMS OTP in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) $30-250/month.
cache: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) $50-300/month.
ml: Separate Python inference service (FastAPI + ONNX Runtime) in the same private network $40-200/month.
observability: Amazon CloudWatch in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) (logs, metrics, alarms) $30-200/month.
Stored data ~500 GB after 12 months at ~$0.02-0.035/GB-month (year-end volume used as an upper bound, not an average).
Phone OTP: 300,000 users x 0.3-1.0 OTP logins/month at SNS India SMS rate band per SMS = $270-1,800/month (long-lived sessions keep OTPs rare).
Spiky traffic: the upper bound is a peak month; with autoscaling, quiet months run near the lower bound.
Excluded: payment gateway fees (~2% per transaction) are a share of revenue, not infrastructure.
Excluded: taxes, domain names, paid support plans and data-egress spikes. Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote.

warnings.message: Every launch user (10,000) is assumed online at once at peak; sizing uses this conservative figure.
RBI payment-data localisation: all payment data, backups and logs stay on systems in India; anything processed abroad must be deleted there and brought back within 24 hours.
PCI DSS v4.0.1: card data handled only by the gateway's hosted fields/checkout keeps scope small (SAQ A when fully outsourced); still secure the pages that embed checkout.

DPDP Act 2023: collect consent with a clear notice, support access/correction/erasure requests, keep breach-notification runbooks (72 h to the Board under the 2025 Rules) and delete data when the purpose ends. Hosting in India simplifies transfers; legal review still required.
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certifies your organisation's ISMS, not a cloud provider's badge: keep asset inventory, access reviews, logging and change management for this system.
Upper estimate $6219/month can exceed the $6000 budget at peak usage.

assumptions: Knowledge base as of 2026-11-11; lifecycle and pricing judgements use that date, not the run date.
Scale tier 'medium' from 300,000 users and ~10,000 peak concurrent users (people, not requests per second; used only for sizing and cost).
